Re: Appeal of prior authorization denial  
Member: Jordan Grant  
Member ID: W874343567  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA — Connecticut  
Requested service: Lumbar fusion  
CPT: 22612  
Reference number: POC-6A6D9C61F2-98168  
Date of denial notice: August 15, 2026

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for the requested lumbar fusion, CPT 22612. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The enclosed records provide the clinical information needed to evaluate the request.

Aetna’s publicly available Clinical Policy Bulletin 0743, “Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion,” states: “Aetna considers the following medically necessary.”

The records address the relevant medical-necessity information as follows:

- Progressive symptoms: I have had nine months of progressive lower-back and leg pain that is not relieved by rest.
- Failure of conservative treatment: I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility exercises, from April 24, 2026, through July 3, 2026, for a total of 20 visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment. I also used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on May 9, 2026, produced only four weeks of partial relief.
- Neurologic symptoms and findings: The examination documents neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes. The symptoms include leg pain and heaviness with standing and walking.
- Imaging correlation: The July 18, 2026, lumbar MRI and flexion-extension radiographs show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.
- Functional limitation: I cannot stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop. The symptoms are relieved by sitting. This substantially limits ordinary standing and walking activities.
- Other clinical information: There is no active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking. BMI is 29, and there is no bowel or bladder dysfunction.

The policy text retrieved from Aetna’s public page also states: “Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated.” The documented neurogenic claudication and bilateral L5 sensory loss correspond to the L4-L5 pathology shown on imaging.

The policy further states: “Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings.” The July 18, 2026, MRI documents severe central stenosis with cauda equina compression at L4-L5, corresponding to the clinical findings.

The policy also states: “Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (unless there is an indication for waiver of requirements for conservative management, noted below).” The enclosed records document 10 weeks and 20 visits of supervised physical therapy, six months of unsuccessful NSAID treatment, and only temporary partial benefit from the corticosteroid injection.

The policy states: “Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression.” The documented inability to stand or walk for more than 10 minutes because of leg pain and heaviness demonstrates this functional limitation.

The policy page also states: “Lumbar spinal fusion for degenerative disc disease and all other indications not listed as medically necessary.” This request is not based on isolated low-back pain or degenerative disc disease alone. It is based on documented L4-L5 degenerative spondylolisthesis with dynamic translation, severe central stenosis, cauda equina compression, neurogenic claudication, bilateral L5 sensory loss, substantial walking and standing limitation, and failure of extensive conservative treatment.

I request that Aetna overturn the denial and approve CPT 22612. If Aetna continues to consider the submission incomplete, please identify each specific missing record or criterion and provide the complete clinical-review criteria, including the version applied to this request and the clinical rationale for the determination.

Please include the enclosed clinical records in the review:

1. July 18, 2026, lumbar MRI report;
2. July 18, 2026, flexion-extension radiograph report;
3. Physical therapy discharge note documenting 20 visits from April 24, 2026, through July 3, 2026;
4. Medication-treatment history documenting six months of NSAID use;
5. May 9, 2026, corticosteroid-injection record;
6. Examination findings documenting neurogenic claudication and diminished bilateral L5 sensation; and
7. The treating surgeon’s clinical documentation from Duval, MD.

Please send the appeal determination to:

Jordan Grant  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address, if applicable]

Thank you for your prompt review.

Sincerely,

Jordan Grant  
Member ID: W874343567
